lede: This week: A24's biggest hit ever crashes onto Max, Sharon Horgan and a career-best Slow Horses deliver the season's sharpest comedy and thriller, a lush Son Ye-jin K-drama and a civilian Traitors spinoff round out the surprises, and an announced slate is led by Lee Chang-dong's long-awaited return and Spielberg's surprise Peacock landing.

shortlist.title: Backrooms
shortlist.meta: Dir. Kane Parsons; with Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve. 110 min.
shortlist.blurb: A24's highest-grossing film ever turns the viral "Backrooms" creepypasta into an unsettling feature: a failing furniture salesman stumbles into an endless maze of liminal rooms, and his therapist follows him in to find out what's really down there.

shortlist.title: The Traitors: New Blood
shortlist.meta: Hosted by Alan Cumming; 22 civilian contestants. Spinoff season, weekly episodes.
shortlist.blurb: The killer social-deduction format swaps celebrities for everyday Americans — a physician, an airline pilot, a funeral director — competing for $250,000 in a Scottish castle, and it's NBC's biggest unscripted premiere in six years.

shortlist.title: Youth
shortlist.meta: Created by and starring Sharon Horgan (Catastrophe). Season 1, weekly episodes.
shortlist.blurb: Sharon Horgan turns her sharp comic voice on midlife instead of new love: a 50-year-old London literary agent navigates divorce, dating, and reinvention in what critics call "spit-takingly funny."

shortlist.title: Neagley
shortlist.meta: With Maria Sten as Frances Neagley (Reacher spinoff). Season 1, 8 episodes, full drop.
shortlist.blurb: The Reacher universe's best supporting player gets her own sharper, more psychologically-driven spinoff, climbing to Certified Fresh as critics call it smarter than expected.

shortlist.title: Slow Horses
shortlist.meta: With Gary Oldman as Jackson Lamb. Season 6, 6 episodes, weekly.
shortlist.blurb: Apple's acclaimed spy thriller returns for its best-reviewed season yet, hitting the highest average critic score of the show's run.

shortlist.title: The Scandal
shortlist.meta: Dir. Jung Ji-woo; with Son Ye-jin, Ji Chang-wook. Limited series, 8 episodes.
shortlist.blurb: A lush, starry Joseon-era adaptation of Untold Scandal (by way of Les Liaisons Dangereuses) pits a brilliant noblewoman against the era's most notorious playboy in an escalating seduction wager.

movies.title: Unabomber
movies.blurb: Russell Crowe and Jacob Tremblay anchor a dual-timeline true-crime drama on Ted Kaczynski's radicalization and the FBI manhunt that followed; reviews are mixed but the performances draw praise.

tv.title: MobLand
tv.blurb: Tom Hardy, Pierce Brosnan, and Helen Mirren return for a stronger, Certified Fresh second season of this British-Irish crime saga about a fracturing mob empire.

tv.title: Paolo
tv.blurb: A French psychological thriller about obsessive fixation on a rising political candidate, praised at Séries Mania for its "Saltburn energy" — the kind of festival-vetted import a US watchlist would never surface.

tv.title: The Final Problem
tv.blurb: A stylish Spanish locked-room mystery adapted from Arturo Pérez-Reverte, stranding suspects in a storm-battered 1959 Majorca hotel for an Agatha Christie-style whodunit.

tv.title: 4 Blocks Zero
tv.blurb: A prequel to the acclaimed German crime drama 4 Blocks, tracing the Hamady family's rise in 1990s Berlin.

tv.title: Delusion
tv.blurb: A Thai mystery weaving dementia, family secrets, and village folklore into a witch-hunt narrative — under-tracked, and reviews call it smarter than it is satisfying.

tv.title: A Different World
tv.blurb: Debbie Allen's HBCU-set sequel to the classic Cosby Show spinoff centers a new Gen Z cast, with Jasmine Guy and Kadeem Hardison reprising their roles.

tv.title: Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars
tv.blurb: Gordon Ramsay's BAFTA-nominated docuseries returns, following 16 restaurants across Europe, the US, and Brazil fighting to earn or keep a Michelin star.

anime.title: A Wild Last Boss Appeared! Season 2
anime.blurb: The overpowered demon-lord-who-just-wants-a-quiet-life comedy returns for a new isekai arc.

anime.title: STEEL BALL RUN: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure — 2nd Stage
anime.blurb: After a controversial mid-run pause sparked fan backlash, JoJo's seventh saga resumes weekly with Johnny Joestar and Gyro Zeppeli's brutal transcontinental horse race.

anime.title: Overgeared
anime.blurb: A Korean LitRPG webcomic adaptation about a blacksmith who becomes overpowered through in-game crafting — early reviews call it "far better than it ever needed to be."

anime.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion
anime.blurb: Hideaki Anno's genre-redefining mecha classic, plus its two film endings, joins Criterion Channel's library this month.

catalog.title: Romería
catalog.blurb: Carla Simón's Cannes-competition drama joins Criterion Channel, following a young woman piecing together her late parents' past.

catalog.title: Our Land
catalog.blurb: Argentine master Lucrecia Martel's documentary arrives on Criterion Channel.

catalog.title: Nadja
catalog.blurb: Michael Almereyda's stylish, David Lynch-produced vampire noir joins Criterion in a newly restored director's cut.

catalog.title: Distant Journey
catalog.blurb: Alfréd Radok's harrowing Czech drama about the Holocaust, blending documentary footage with expressionist staging, joins Criterion's library.

catalog.title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
catalog.blurb: Tarantino's shaggy, loving ode to late-'60s Hollywood lands on Prime Video ahead of its upcoming sequel.

announced.title: Ink
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed a Jan. 8 streaming date for Danny Boyle's Venice-premiered drama on the birth of Rupert Murdoch's tabloid empire, starring Jack O'Connell and Guy Pearce.

announced.title: Possible Love
announced.blurb: Lee Chang-dong's first film in eight years — a Venice Grand Jury Prize and FIPRESCI winner starring Jeon Do-yeon — gets a confirmed Nov. 6 global Netflix date.

announced.title: Disclosure Day
announced.blurb: Peacock confirmed an exclusive streaming debut for Spielberg's UFO-disclosure thriller, starring Emily Blunt and Josh O'Connor — his biggest box office hit since Ready Player One.

announced.title: Carrie
announced.blurb: Mike Flanagan's full reinvention of Stephen King's Carrie dropped its full trailer this week, confirming all 8 episodes land Oct. 7.

announced.title: The Invite
announced.blurb: A24's Sundance-breakout relationship dramedy from Olivia Wilde, starring Seth Rogen, Edward Norton, and Penélope Cruz, gets a confirmed HBO Max streaming date.

announced.title: The Death of Robin Hood
announced.blurb: Michael Sarnoski's (Pig) revisionist Robin Hood, starring Hugh Jackman and Bill Skarsgård, confirmed an Oct. 16 HBO Max date after a rocky theatrical run.

announced.title: Masterplan
announced.blurb: Amazon MGM unveiled the trailer for this Mona Lisa heist film starring Stanley Tucci and Simona Tabasco, confirming an Oct. 16 Prime Video date.

announced.title: Quiztopia
announced.blurb: Netflix unveiled cast and a teaser for this Japanese dystopian thriller — a constitutionally-mandated, lethal quiz show — confirming a Dec. 17 global premiere.

announced.title: 100 Days of Deception
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed an Oct. 10 date for this Korean period espionage thriller set in 1932 Japanese-occupied Gyeongseong, starring Kim You-jung.
